A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from DiffRatio-MoD to DiffCR. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image and inpainting experiments, including generation quality, computational efficiency, ablations, visual examples and model-based human-preference scores.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds MS-COCO-30K caching-baseline comparisons and a compression-ratio ablation in Appendices H and J.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same token router, adjacent-bin interpolation, nearest-bin inference and MSE compression objective under the DiffCR rename. The additional full-model timesteps are presented as a setting for the new Appendix J experiment; no revision to the general framework is specified.

E1.justification: Appendices H and J add MS-COCO-30K evaluation for text-to-image generation. The existing internal inpainting dataset, LAION datasets and two generation tasks are retained, making this a focused benchmark extension.

E2.justification: Appendix H newly reports comparisons against L2C and TGATE. Existing comparison methods remain in the original experiments. DeepCache and CMYC receive qualitative characterizations in Table 4, without reported performance results.

E3.justification: The new caching comparison targets approximately 25% latency savings. The compression sweep uses batch size 16 and reserves one third of timesteps for full-model inference. Table 1 also corrects its caption from batch sizes 1/16 to 16/128, matching the unchanged column headings; this does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix J and Table 6 add a focused sensitivity study measuring FID, CLIP score and latency at 0%, 10%, 30%, 50%, 70% and 90% compression. Existing component ablations, router visualizations and training-trajectory analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. The additional experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original table values remain unchanged, including inpainting preference scores moved from Table 4 to Table 5. Appendix H adds FID 28.6 for both DiffCR and L2C versus 43.6 for TGATE. Table 6 adds compression-sweep results, including FID 27.80/29.21 and latency 11.90/7.12 seconds at 0%/90%. Section 4.3 replaces the 44.08/207.01 FID-reduction summary with 323.13/229.01 explicitly for T2I, consistent with retained Table 1 values.

T1.justification: The mathematical description of ratio interpolation and the MSE objective is retained. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations are added; the new loss discussion is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the three-part contribution, the claim of applying MoD to vision, and the generation-quality versus efficiency claim, including the 8.51 average FID reduction. Renaming and rephrasing do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendices B and K explain how competing losses prevent uniformly zero compression and discuss polarized router outputs without enforced binary predictions. Appendix H explains compatibility with temporal caching, while Appendix J interprets higher compression under partially uncompressed inference. Its claimed FID increase below 1 overstates the 90% result.

D1.justification: Appendices B and K explicitly disclose the absence of additional regularization and enforced binary router predictions. The first-page project hyperlink changes from the DiffRatio-MoD page to the DiffCR page. Existing optimizer, LoRA and hardware details remain unchanged; external resource availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for COCO and temporal attention decomposition, plus a focused comparison with caching approaches in Appendix H and Table 4. The broader positioning remains stable. The new CMYC discussion cites reference 25, whose bibliography entry concerns DNS time-to-live, leaving an internal citation mismatch.

P1.justification: The framework is renamed throughout, wording receives localized edits, and Appendices H, J and K are added. The former Appendix H becomes I. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the caching-characteristics table and compression-ablation table. The retained inpainting preference table becomes Table 5 and moves, Figure 13 is repositioned, and figure labels and captions reflect the renamed method. Existing plots and qualitative examples are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added COCO comparisons and compression sweep provide useful evidence about alternative accelerators and operating limits, while the batch-size caption and FID-summary corrections improve consistency. The gains are limited by sparse new protocol details and an overstatement in Appendix J: Table 6 shows a 1.41 FID increase at 90% compression, despite the claim of an increase below 1. These weaknesses temper the improvement without undermining the retained core evidence.
